label: tfim_6

card.name: majorana_symmetry_block_diagonalization
card.precondition: family = dv_angle (Clifford+Rz op list), 2 <= n_qubits <= 14, needs rotations, measurement_free. The op list must be Gaussian in the Jordan-Wigner sense: `v4.api.fermion.is_gaussian(ops)` is true, i.e. every rotation's front-frame Pauli is a Majorana bilinear i*g_a*g_b (`bilinear_of` succeeds for all of them) and the residual Clifford is a signed Majorana permutation. Fires only when the current off-grid rotation count exceeds the symmetry-reduced Givens count computed below. Circuits that are not free-fermion are excluded and cost nothing.
card.identity: A Gaussian circuit acts on the 2n Majoranas as one real orthogonal R in O(2n) (`orthogonal_of(ops)`); the existing free-fermion rule realises R by a plain Givens network, which needs 2n(2n-1)/2 plane rotations (66 for n=6) because that is dim SO(2n). Reduce that count with a SYMMETRY instead. Let S be a signed permutation of the Majoranas with S^2 = I (an involution). Every such S is a Gaussian Clifford (it maps Pauli strings to Pauli strings), so applying it is free of rotations. If R commutes with S, then R preserves each eigenspace V_+ , V_- of S, of dimensions d_+ + d_- = 2n. Let B be the orthogonal change of basis into those eigenspaces. Then B^T R B = R_+ (+) R_- is block diagonal, and R = B (R_+ (+) R_-) B^T. Givens-decompose each block separately: d_+(d_+ -1)/2 + d_-(d_- -1)/2 plane rotations instead of 2n(2n-1)/2. For a balanced split of 12 that is 15 + 15 = 30 instead of 66. B itself is free: the eigenvectors of an involutive signed permutation are (e_j +- S e_j)/sqrt(2) on each 2-cycle {j, S(j)} and e_j on each fixed point, so B is a product of plane rotations by exactly pi/4 in the planes (j, S(j)) -- angles on the pi/4 grid, which gridsynth never pays for (they emit Clifford/T directly through `with_ops`). Procedure: (1) R = orthogonal_of(ops); (2) enumerate a declared finite family of involutive signed Majorana permutations S -- site reflection j -> n+1-j about the chain centre, half-chain translation, global Majorana sign flips g_{2i-1} -> -g_{2i-1}, and their products -- each as a 12x12 signed permutation with S^2 = I; (3) keep those with ||R S - S R||_F < 1e-9; (4) for each kept S compute the Givens count of the block form, take the S minimising it; (5) re-emit the circuit as B, then `givens(R_+)` and `givens(R_-)` on the block coordinates, then B^T, then the residual sign diagonal, via `fermion.emit` / `plane_rotation`; (6) keep the candidate only if the off-grid rotation count strictly falls.
card.correctness: Exact, no error drawn. (i) The map from a Gaussian circuit to R in O(2n) is a group homomorphism and is faithful up to global phase, so reproducing the same R (and the same residual sign diagonal / parity sector) reproduces the same unitary up to global phase -- this is the same correctness argument the existing free-fermion rule already relies on, only the factorisation of R changes. (ii) [R,S] = 0 with S^2 = I implies R preserves ker(S-I) and ker(S+I), the standard isotypic decomposition (Schur); hence B^T R B is block diagonal with orthogonal blocks, exactly. (iii) B is orthogonal and is itself a signed-permutation-conjugated product of pi/4 plane rotations, so B and B^T are exactly representable with on-grid angles. (iv) Each block is realised by its own exact Givens (QR) factorisation, which is exact arithmetic on a d x d orthogonal matrix. (v) The judge still checks the whole circuit against the original: the rewrite is unitary-exact up to global phase, and the only residual error is the usual gridsynth error on the surviving rotations, which is cheaper because there are fewer of them (eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz actually grows, a second-order extra saving I do not claim).
card.trigger: `is_gaussian(ops)` is true AND R = `orthogonal_of(ops)` commutes (Frobenius residual < 1e-9) with at least one involutive signed Majorana permutation S from the declared family, whose eigenspace split (d_+, d_-) gives d_+(d_+ -1)/2 + d_-(d_- -1)/2 < (number of current off-grid rotations). On tfim_6: 66 off-grid rotations, 12 Majorana planes; the uniform transverse-field Ising chain is reflection symmetric (and, if the boundary is periodic, also translation symmetric), so site reflection should commute with R and split 12 into 6 + 6.
card.expected_effect: The 66 distinct off-grid Rz rotations (the full generic SO(12) Givens network, 66 * ~50.8 T = 3354 T, which is the entire current cost) are replaced by two 6-dimensional Givens networks: 15 + 15 = 30 off-grid rotations, plus the basis change B and B^T, which are ~12 plane rotations at exactly pi/4 and so emit a handful of Clifford/T gates with no gridsynth cost. Net 36 fewer synthesized rotations at ~50.8 T each.
card.source: Jordan-Wigner / matchgate Gaussian circuit compilation: Kivlichan et al., 'Quantum simulation of electronic structure with linear depth and connectivity', PRL 120, 110501 (2018); Jiang, Sung, Kechedzhi, Smelyanskiy, Boixo, 'Quantum algorithms to simulate many-body physics of correlated fermions', PRApplied 9, 044036 (2018); Clements et al., Optica 3, 1460 (2016) for the Givens network; symmetry-adapted (isotypic) block diagonalization of a commuting orthogonal matrix, standard representation theory, as used for the exactly-solvable TFIM after Pfeuty (1970).

label: hhl_8

card.name: template_descent_block_resynthesis
card.precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz and two_qubit; min_qubits 2, max_qubits 20; applies to any Clifford+Rz op list that partitions into width<=4 blocks containing at least 2 cx and at least 3 rotations. Circuits without multi-qubit blocks (pure 1-qubit chains) are excluded and cost nothing.
card.identity: Skeleton-shrinking block resynthesis (template descent + instantiation), as opposed to angle fixing on a fixed skeleton. For each block B from blocks.partition(circuit, width<=4, max_gates=40): (1) form the exact local unitary U = sim.unitary(B.local_ops, B.k) (k<=4, so at most 16x16); (2) take B's own Clifford skeleton as template T0 and enumerate reduced templates T1, T2, ... by deleting ONE two-qubit gate at a time (and the rotation slots that become adjacent-mergeable), ordered by the deleted cx's contribution to the block's entangling power (smallest first), each reduced template re-expressed by refit.euler_template with one rz slot per surviving single-qubit position; (3) for each candidate template, fit its angle vector by refit.least_squares against U from several deterministic restarts (the previous template's fitted angles with the deleted slot's angle set to 0, plus a fixed pseudo-random restart set), giving Fit(angles, distance); (4) accept the SMALLEST template whose fitted phase-aligned operator distance is <= the block's share d_B of the drawn budget and whose priced cost (T-count under eps_rz = eps_synth/N_Rz, then qubits, then CNOT) is strictly lower than the block's current cost; recurse (try to delete one more two-qubit gate from the accepted template) until no candidate fits; (5) on the survivor only, spend the block's unspent remainder with refit.pin_to_grid to push any further angles onto the pi/4 grid. Splice back with blocks.splice. The distinguishing step is (2)+(3): DPF keeps the skeleton fixed and only moves angles; this REPLACES the skeleton with a strictly shorter one whenever the block's true reachable-manifold dimension is below the parameter count TKET's peephole output happens to carry, and refits ALL angles, not just the unpinned ones.
card.correctness: Each partition block is dependency-contiguous, so substituting its local op list by any V is a valid rewrite of the whole circuit: the global unitary changes from ... U ... to ... V ..., and by unitary invariance and subadditivity of the operator norm the end-to-end phase-aligned distance is bounded by the sum of the per-block distances ||V_B - U_B||_op (phase-aligned, since global phase is unobservable). Each accepted block therefore charges exactly its measured distance d_B to the shared ledger, and sum_B d_B <= the amount drawn. The fits themselves are not trusted: sim.hs_distance on the exact 2^k x 2^k matrices gives the number the frozen judge will charge, and the judge re-verifies every application (phase-aligned operator distance on the changed window, plus the one whole-circuit check per pass against the ORIGINAL circuit), so a template whose least-squares fit is a local minimum that does not reach U is simply rejected, never accepted on the optimizer's word. Soundness of the descent order does not matter for correctness, only for how much it finds: deleting a cx can only shrink the reachable set, so a fit that succeeds certifies that U lies on the smaller template's manifold to within d_B.
card.trigger: Run over blocks.blocks_with_rotations(circuit, minimum=3) restricted to blocks with k >= 2 and at least 2 two-qubit gates. A block is a match iff at least one reduced template reaches fitted distance <= its share AND the priced cost strictly falls; the number of off-grid rotations in the replacement must be strictly smaller than in the block (pure cx reductions at equal rotation count are also kept, since cost order breaks ties on CNOT). Blocks with 0 or 1 two-qubit gates, or whose best reduced fit stalls above its share, are skipped with no edit and no spend (budget.trial / refund around every attempt).
card.expected_effect: hhl_8 after the book has 439 off-grid rotations at eps_rz = 2.28e-6, i.e. ~57 T each, which is essentially all of the 26137. The circuit is TKET-FullPeepholeOptimise'd output of unitary-synthesised HHL blocks (693 h, 547 cx, 419 distinct generic angles, trigrams 'h rz h' and 'h s cx'): TKET squashes single-qubit chains and does 2-qubit KAK, but never resynthesises width-3/4 blocks, so structured HHL blocks (controlled eigenvalue-inversion rotations, QFT phase ladders) are carried in skeletons with more cx and more rotation slots than their true manifold needs. Each deleted cx typically removes 1-3 rotation slots. Expect ~80 off-grid rotations removed (439 -> ~360), which also lowers eps_rz' = 5e-4/360 and so the per-rotation gridsynth cost, landing near 21-22k T; the cx count falls too (secondary cost key). Nearly all of the drawn error is insurance: on blocks that really are over-parameterised the fit reaches ~1e-12, so the realised spend should be far below 2.5e-4, leaving the rest of the pool for other rules.
card.source: Younis, Sen, Yelick, Iancu, 'QFAST / QSearch: Quantum circuit synthesis by topology-aware template descent' (2020-2021) and Davis et al., 'Towards optimal topology-aware quantum circuit synthesis' (QSearch/LEAP, BQSKit) - template enumeration plus numerical instantiation (QFactor) of a fixed skeleton; the Cartan/KAK parameter-count bound (Vidal-Dawson, Shende-Bullock-Markov) is what makes a deleted cx a real dimension drop.
